ca_vector_boulder.blurb: Vector Boulder is a large block in Culp Valley, San Diego County, standing in plain view beside the road at roughly 3,000 feet. It is a small bouldering stop with eleven problems, spread from the easiest grades through to a few hard ones, so there is something for a beginner and a handful of projects for a strong climber. The easy lines are the popular ones, and several smaller boulders sit close by. Nothing about the stop is remote: you can pull up near the block and be on the rock almost immediately, which makes it an easy add-on to a desert day.
ca_vector_boulder.parking_note: Take Culp Valley Road toward its T-junction; the boulder comes into view on the left just before you reach it, and you can leave the car close by.
ca_vector_boulder.approach: A very short walk of a few minutes from the roadside pullout to the boulder.

ca_ranger_rock.blurb: Ranger Rock is one of the smaller boulders in the Buttermilks Main zone, in the Buttermilk Country west of Bishop at about 6,400 feet. It holds eleven problems, all on a single block, mostly easy to moderate with a couple of harder lines near the top end. The rock is granodiorite and the block is easy to spot from the west parking area, making it a gentle place to warm up before moving on to bigger neighbours. The landings across this part of the Buttermilks are flat and sandy.
ca_ranger_rock.approach: Walk east from the west parking area; the boulder is visible from there.

ca_stoned_wheat_thin_cliff.blurb: Stoned Wheat Thin Cliff is the tall face on Main Island in Clark Canyon, in the Mammoth Lakes area of the Eastern Sierra, at about 7,500 feet. Walls here run past 200 feet, so routes are long and sustained, with a few spread over several pitches. The pocketed stone is rough and grippy. Most of the eleven lines are bolted, with a couple of trad options, and nearly all sit in the 5.10 range with a few easier and harder ones. Sun reaches the face, though tall pines can cast shade at times, and the cliff is fairly secluded for such a developed canyon.
ca_stoned_wheat_thin_cliff.approach: From the lot, follow the climbers' trail past the boulder, take the left branch at the split and go steeply uphill to the island's base.

ca_starr_wall.blurb: Starr Wall is a small high-elevation crag above Rock Creek Road in the Eastern Sierra, around 10,500 feet, set among aspens with creek views. Eleven mixed trad and sport lines, mostly 50 to 70 feet, run from roughly 5.8 through the low 5.13s, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. The stone is generally sound, though loose flakes are worth watching for. The wall faces southeast, so it warms in the morning and loses the sun by early afternoon, which keeps it comfortable at altitude. It is quiet, and the short climb in is an easy price for the setting.
ca_starr_wall.parking_note: Use the small dirt pullout on the right just before the Rock Creek bridge, about ten miles up Rock Creek Road from Tom's Place.
ca_starr_wall.approach: Pick up the cairns heading southwest through the aspens, hop the little creek, and climb benches to the pack trail. Follow it briefly south, then break west at more cairns to the wall. Roughly 400 feet of gain.

ca_weekend_retreat.blurb: Weekend Retreat is a tucked-away alcove of boulders inside the Catacombs, on the Sherwin Plateau above the Owens River Gorge, near Mammoth Lakes. It is a shady pocket of tuff with eleven problems that run from very easy to a couple at about V2, so it suits anyone wanting a relaxed warm-up. The rock is pocketed, and landings across the Catacombs are mostly flat pumice. Reach it by walking up the wash and finding the alcove entrance. It is secluded, an ideal calm start to a day of wandering among the formations.
ca_weekend_retreat.approach: From Devil Boulder follow the wash north; the alcove opens about thirty yards beyond Tower Boulder.

ca_byron_s_boulder.blurb: Byron’s Boulder is a single boulder beside the highway on the slopes of Mount Shasta, at around 5,000 feet. Eleven problems cover most of the lower grades, from warm-ups on its easiest faces up to a few V3 lines on the back side. It is an easy find and a friendly spot for beginners or a quick session while in town for the mountain, though there is only one block, so plan it as a short stop rather than a full day. Landings and sun exposure are not documented, so bring pads and look it over before committing.

ca_slander_crag.blurb: Slander Crag is a sport crag in the Sub Gorge section of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop, just under 5,000 feet. It faces east, so it takes strong morning sun and falls into shade later, which makes it the best-lit cliff of its neighbours and a good option on warm days. Its eleven bolted lines are mostly 5.10, with a few 5.11 and 5.12 routes above, and they are single pitch. The setting is close to the river and feels remote, and it draws fewer people than the busier gorge walls.

ca_west_face_12.blurb: The West Face of Lembert Dome is a short slab above the Tuolumne Meadows picnic lot in Yosemite, at around 8,600 feet. It holds about ten routes, mostly trad with some top-rope lines and a single bolted one, ranging from 5.7 to 5.11 and clustered between 5.8 and 5.10. Climbs are typically two or three pitches, and several finish at a shared ledge with anchors, so you can lap a number of routes quickly. It is only a couple of minutes from the car, which makes it a handy objective for a short day.
ca_west_face_12.parking_note: Leave the car in the paved Lembert Dome picnic area lot, directly below the face.
ca_west_face_12.approach: The face rises above the lot; it is a walk of about two minutes straight to the base.
